sentences.text: This is the first application filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail relating to FIR No.275/2022 dated 08.09.2022 registered at Police Station Sausar, District Chhindwara, for the offence under Sections 420, 409, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The applicant is in jail since 06.03.2023.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that as per the allegation made by the complainant and the story narrated by the prosecution, the present applicant at the relevant point of time when alleged fraud has been committed was working as Manager in the company and he accompanied the other accused persons in the conspiracy of fraud alleged to have been committed by them.

The counsel for the applicant submits that the incident occurred somewhere in the year 2008-2009, but this fraud was disclosed at later point of time when the Income Tax Department made some enquiry Vinay Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123715010/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and as such, facts have been disclosed that false information was given to the Income Tax Department and then only the complainant lodged FIR against the present applicant.
He submits that the present applicant being the Manager of the company has been terminated from services on 18.03.2019.

He submits that even otherwise, when the applicant was arrested, charge-sheet had already been filed and one of the co-accused persons namely Pawan Jain has already granted bail by this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.

Further, the other co-accused namely Ajay Khandelwal has also been granted interim protection by the Supreme Court and at this stage keeping the applicant behind the bars would not serve any purpose and, therefore, application needs to be considered.

On the other hand, the counsel for the State has opposed the submission made by the counsel for the applicant and submitted that looking to the allegations made and period of custody, though co-accused namely Pawan Jain has been granted bail, but keeping him in custody for some long period, therefore, at this stage, the bail application of the present applicant deserves to be dismissed because he was arrested only on 06.03.2023.
He submits even otherwise, the present applicant has past criminal antecedents relating to same nature of offence.

The counsel for the objector has also opposed the submission made by the counsel for the applicant and submitted that co-accused Pawan Jain has been granted bail by this Court considering the fact on wrong premise because the charge-sheet on the date of submitting the application was not filed by the prosecution.
Further, anticipatory bail has also not been granted to co-accused Ajay Khandelwal by the Supreme Court, but only the interim protection has been granted.
He submits that the bail granted to other co-accused persons cannot be made basis for granting bail to the present applicant.
He prays that the bail application may kindly be dismissed.

He placed reliance upon a decision of the Supreme Court reported in (2017) 15 SCC 574 parties being (Rukmani Mahato Vs. State of Jharkhand) and also upon a decision of this Court passed in M.Cr.C.
No.2743/2018 (State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Manoj Jatav) saying that the applicant is not entitled to claim parity with other co-accused persons.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, although I am not inclined to grant the benefit of parity to the present applicant, but inclined to consider this application on the ground that the applicant is in jail since 06.03.2023, the incident is of 2008-2009, one of the co- accused persons has already been granted bail by this Court, case is based upon documentary evidence, no further interrogation of the present applicant is required, keeping the present applicant behind the bars would not serve any purpose and as such, this bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance on the dates given by it.

I t is further directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 437(3)
of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
